author: Shrai Popat in Washington
description:
Katie Zacharia tells Guardian her first, widely panned, press briefing followed six-day sprint to appoint her to key role

Donald Trump’s new White House press secretary says it is “unknown” how much she will engage with the press, or hold briefings with reporters, as she faces mounting questions over her legal credentials.

In a brief interview with the Guardian on Thursday, Katie Zacharia detailed the whirlwind sprint to replace her predecessor Karoline Leavitt as the US president’s chief spokesperson.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s new press secretary says it’s ‘unknown’ how much she’ll deal with media

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
At least two people have been hospitalized, and police say suspected shooter was killed at the scene

Multiple people, including children, were injured in a Thursday shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, police confirmed during a press conference.

The suspected gunman is dead, according to Bend police spokesperson Sheila Miller.

Continue reading...
title: Multiple people, including children, injured in elementary school shooting in Oregon

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Witnesses report at least six explosions near palace used by Yemen's internationally recognized government

At least six explosions struck on Thursday near the palace used by Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the port city of Aden, witnesses said.

An official told the Associated Press that at least two people were killed, and Iran-backed Houthi rebels based in northern Yemen quickly claimed responsibility. Government military sources in Yemen told Agence-France Press (AFP) that at least four people were killed and 10 wounded.

Continue reading...
title: Houthi missiles strike Saudi-led coalition forces HQ at presidential palace in Aden

author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
description:
UK defence secretary trying to cool tensions and is arguing it is in America’s economic interests to support Kyiv

Wes Streeting urged the US to stand by Ukraine on his visit to the American capital and sought to cool tensions between the two countries in the wake of the Starlink row that is threatening to set back Kyiv’s war effort.

The British defence secretary, giving a speech before a meeting with his US counterpart, Pete Hegseth, argued that supporting Ukraine was in the long-term interests of Washington, and a business opportunity.

Continue reading...
title: Wes Streeting urges US to back Ukraine on Washington visit after Starlink row

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Voting registration organizations accuse Texas officials of failing to ensure eligible voters can register properly

Texas election officials are struggling to process a massive backlog of nearly 600,000 voter registration applications after a major state computer system failure, just days before early voting is set to open on Monday and amid concerns about widespread voter suppression.

The disruption has raised serious concerns about the state’s voter registration system, with voting rights organizations accusing Texas officials of failing to ensure that eligible voters could properly register.

Continue reading...
title: Texas sued after glitch delays almost 600,000 voter registrations

author: Maya Yang
description:
Prosecutors say Adan Manzano was victim of Danette Colbert’s operation targeting New Orleans tourists

A woman involved in a New Orleans criminal enterprise that targeted tourists and led to the death of a reporter has been resentenced to life.

On Wednesday, a Jefferson Parish judge resentenced 49-year old Danette Colbert to life in prison plus 75 years under Louisiana’s habitual offender law. In September, Colbert was sentenced to a total of 60 years in prison, 50 years for racketeering and a consecutive 10 years for negligent homicide in the death of Adan Manzano, a journalist for the Spanish-language news outlet Telemundo Kansas City.

Contin
title: Woman resentenced to life in prison for death of Kansas City reporter

author: Ariana Baio and agencies
description:
Election officers in Louisiana and Oklahoma receive a powdery substance, prompting evacuations

The FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service are investigating letters sent to state officials and election offices across the country containing an “unknown substance”.

Just weeks before November’s US midterm elections, election officers in Louisiana and Oklahoma received envelopes containing a powdery substance, leading to evacuations. A similar package containing white powder was also sent to the Ohio secretary of state, but the US Postal Service intercepted the package.

Continue reading...
title: FBI investigates letters with ‘unknown substance’ sent to US election officials

author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
description:
Nato source says drones came from Russia, while Romania’s president says attacking commercial ships ‘is unacceptable and has to stop’

Seven sailors are missing after drones struck two tankers near Romania’s Black Sea ⁠coast, setting them ablaze and raising ⁠fresh security concerns on a ​vital shipping route used by Ukraine.

A Nato military source told Reuters the drones that hit the Wine Trader and the Yara J came from Russia. “The drones that caused ⁠the fires on board two tankers inside Romanian territorial waters were of Russian origin,” the source said.

Continue reading...
title: Seven sailors missing after drones strike tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Elon Musk has spent $158m in a month to back Republicans in midterm races – with his efforts mostly focused on Texas

Tens of millions of dollars are pouring into Texas as Democrats stage an audacious bid to win a US Senate seat in the Republican stronghold.

Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, is among those wading into the closely watched race as November’s midterm elections approach.

Continue reading...
title: Paxton v Talarico: tens of millions of dollars pour into closely watched Texas Senate race

author: Associated Press
description:
Rewritten indictment accuses ex-Venezuela president and wife Cilia Flores of leading campaign of torture

Nicolás Maduro insisted on Thursday during an appearance in a New York court that torture allegations in a rewritten drug trafficking indictment against the deposed Venezuelan president and his wife were “false accusations”.

Maduro, shackled at the ankles, was brought to court to face the new charges accusing the couple of leading a state-sponsored campaign of repression that tortured scores of victims, including three Americans.

Continue reading...
title: Nicolás Maduro tells New York court new torture allegations are ‘false’

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
Grid operator is paying huge sums to switch off windfarms in areas of excess electricity generation while turning on gas plants elsewhere

The cost of balancing Great Britain’s power grid has soared to near-record highs of almost £50m a day after windfarms were turned off due to bottlenecks in transmitting power around the country.

The grid operator paid £47.9m on Wednesday to turn windfarms off in areas with an oversupply of electricity and turn gas plants on in areas where supplies were tight.

Continue reading...
title: Cost of balancing Great Britain’s power grid reaches nearly £50m a day

author: Andrew Pulver
description:
The much-loved central London institution, which has been threatened with closure since January 2025, secures 25-year lease without break clause with current landlords

The celebrated Prince Charles repertory cinema in London’s Leicester Square has announced that the threat of closure has been staved off by signing a new 25-year lease with its landlords.

In a post on social media titled “You Saved the PCC”, the cinema said that “after 21 months of uncertainty, we’re delighted to have secured the future of the cinema” and that they had “signed a new 25-year lease with no break clause, ensuring our projectors will keep rolling for years to come”.

Continue reading...
title: Cult venue Prince Charles cinema ‘saved’ after lease renewal signed

author: John Crace
description:
How dare the channel reveal more racism and bigotry within Reform just as he was planning a press conference?

Sometimes the world can be very unfair. As though life is just one cruel joke. How else to make sense of everything? For when the history books come to be written, Nigel Farage will go down as one of the century’s unluckiest politicians.

Poor Nige. All he has ever wanted is a better Britain. A country united in a shared vision where everyone gets along with one another. Where people of all faiths and none look out for each other. Where men and women of all colours are treated as equals. Where Nige can teach the world to sing in perfect harmony.

Continue reading...
title: Just as Saint Nige thought it was safe to reappear, along comes pesky ITV | John Crace

author: Daniel Boffey in Port Stanley, Falkland Islands
description:
Santiago Caputo cites election of Sagal Abdi-Wali as MP and calls UK a threat to the west in post shared by Argentina’s president

The chief adviser to Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has cited the election of Sagal Abdi-Wali to the UK parliament as evidence of the Islamisation of Britain and further reason for Argentina to take sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.

In a post on social media, Santiago Caputo, who is reportedly taking a key role in Argentina’s strategy over the Falklands, suggested that the taking of the south Atlantic islands was necessary to prevent the “interference of an Islamic state” in the region.

Continue reading...
title: Milei adviser claims UK being ‘colonised by Islam’ as Falklands row grows

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Michael Desronvil tells Fox News he never had reasonable doubt Clancy was guilty but didn’t back up his claims

Michael Desronvil, the sole holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy trial has spoken in his first interview since a mistrial was declared.

Desronvil spoke of “tense deliberations” in the jury room, and about how his strong Christian faith helped prepare him for those discussions.

Continue reading...
title: Holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy trial gives first interview since mistrial

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Party chair calls on Labour groups to end local deals if Green councillors do not reject motion attacked as ‘antisemitic’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Labour councils who share power with the Greens have been told to terminate agreements if their Green partners do not condemn the party’s new “Zionism is racism” policy.

Bridget Phillipson, the Labour chair, said groups working with Green party politicians must “review” their agreements and end them unless they reject the controversial motion, which Andy Burnham called “antisemitic”.

Derbyshire Dales Lib De
title: Labour councils told to end agreements with Greens who do not condemn ‘Zionism is racism’ policy

author: Adam Morton and Sarah Basford Canales
description:
Madeleine King told press club emissions from NT fossil fuel basin ‘are accounted for and offset’ but research found 95% of emissions this decade would not have to be offset

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

The resources minister, Madeleine King, is facing calls to correct her claim in a major speech that all greenhouse gas emissions from developing a massive fossil fuel basin in the Northern Territory will be offset to limit their impact on the climate.

Speaking at the National Press Club in Canberra on Wednesday, King defended her support for the development of the Beetaloo gas basin south of Darwin after being asked if she was comfortable with the impact that the emissions from the gas would have on Australians.
title: Resources minister faces calls to correct her claim all Beetaloo emissions will be offset

author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles
description:
Hadid and Jenan Matari withdraw book planned for young readers after disputes with editors over characterizations of 7 October

A book on Palestine for young readers was pulled at Penguin Random House just before its scheduled release, following editorial disputes between the publisher and the book’s Palestinian American authors over their account of Palestinian history.

In November 2024, Random House Children’s Books, a division of Penguin Random House, signed the book deal with Alana Hadid, a philanthropist, activist and older sister of models Bella and Gigi, and Jenan Matari, an author and communications strategist. The book was promoted for release in September this year.

Continue reading...
title: Palestine book co-written by Alana Hadid pulled from Random House just before release

author: Ben Smee
description:
The controversial legislation may end up placing large sections of its suburban support – critical to the party’s lead in the polls – on the bonfire

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

For almost two years, the Liberal National party’s strategy for government in Queensland has been to stay well clear of issues that risk burning through political capital.

On Wednesday, one of the most tentative conservative governments in recent history announced plans for sweeping and controversial changes to workplace laws.

Continue reading...
title: Queensland’s LNP has tread softly in government. It’s now baring its teeth over the power to break up workers’ strikes

author: Emine Sinmaz
description:
Southwark crown court jury is shown video of woman telling detectives about alleged attack in 1999

A woman has alleged Russell Brand told her “it’s just fun” as he raped her in a hotel room at the 1999 Labour party conference, a court has heard.

The alleged victim told detectives the comedian made her feel sick and dirty as he assaulted her despite her pleading: “Get off me, please stop. It hurts.”

Continue reading...
title: Russell Brand told woman ‘it’s just fun’ as he raped her, court hears

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Move comes as Senator Elizabeth Warren condemns Barclays response to questions over ex-boss’s ties to sex offender

US lawmakers have unveiled a new bill to hold Wall Street’s “Epstein-connected” bosses to account for helping finance the late sex offender’s crimes.

It came as top Democratic senator Elizabeth Warren condemned the UK bank Barclays for “dodging responsibility” over its failure to vet former boss Jes Staley and his ties to the once well-connected billionaire.

Continue reading...
title: US lawmakers unveil bill to hold Wall Street’s ‘Epstein-connected’ bosses to account

author: Presented by Kiran Stacey and Peter Walker, produced by May Robson, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
description:
Andy Burnham is being accused of a serious misjudgment over his comments about meetings with Manchester City’s owners. Kiran Stacey discusses the controversy after returning from a trade trip to India with the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, and the new Greater Manchester mayor, Bev Craig, during which Stacey discovered that a representative of the football club was also present. The club was recently found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League rules. What could the fallout mean for Burnham?

You can watch Politics Weekly on our YouTube channel here
title: Is Andy Burnham in hot water over Manchester City? – podcast

author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
description:
Officials issue guidance saying the ammonia in animal urine should be watered down to stop it corroding bark

A neighbourhood in Vienna has introduced guidelines for dog walking, including the use of bottled tap water to rinse away urine and protect vulnerable trees.

Neubau, an up-and-coming, densely populated district dotted with cafes and galleries, rolled out the Schönes Gassi (nice dog walk) campaign this week.

Continue reading...
title: Bring a bottle: Viennese dog owners told to dilute their pets’ urine to protect trees

author: Steven Morris
description:
Exclusive: Portsmouth Historic Dockyard’s new £15m permanent display tells tales of courage from conflicts such as Crimean and both world wars

They tell tales of bravery under fire, may lead to conversations about the UK’s place in the world and could prompt visitors to reflect on what they might have done if faced with the same perilous circumstances.

All 10 Victoria Crosses (VCs) awarded to members of the Royal Marines are going on display together for the first time along with tales of courage during conflicts such as the Crimean and both world wars.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Fantastically special’: all 10 Victoria Crosses awarded to Royal Marines go on show for first time

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Discovery of grenades prompted a neighborhood lockdown and a visit from the Austin police department’s bomb squad

A buyer at a Texas estate sale discovered several second world war-era grenades in a box of newly bought items, prompting a neighborhood lockdown and a visit from the Austin police department’s bomb squad.

The grenades, which were described as “live and active” in a social media post by the Austin police association, were removed and disarmed.

Continue reading...
title: Texas resident discovers second world war-era grenades in box bought at estate sale

author: Reuters
description:
Authorities say suspect, 19, was allegedly planning a mass shooting and had shared a white supremacist manifesto

A man arrested in a Chicago suburb had shared a ⁠document expressing white supremacist views and outlined an alleged plan to carry out a mass shooting, potentially targeting a Hindu place of worship, police ⁠said on Wednesday.

Alexandros Paporakis, 19, was ​arrested on Sunday after an individual reported receiving concerning electronic communications from him, Palatine police said. It was not immediately clear if he had ⁠legal representation.

Continue reading...
title: Illinois man arrested over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship, police say

author: Sandra Laville
description:
Some reservoirs in south-east and south-west at critically low levels as water companies call for non-essential user bans on businesses

A severe drought has been declared in six areas of England with some reservoirs at critically low levels, threatening public supplies.

Parts of Devon, Cornwall, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex and West Sussex have moved into severe drought, and urgent measures are being taken to secure public supplies of water after the UK experienced its hottest summer on record.

Continue reading...
title: Severe drought declared in six areas of England as public water supplies under threat

author: Eduardo Porter
description:
Voters’ opposition to the state of Trump’s economy is well established – despite his desperate attempts to deflect

It’s indisputable that the political polarization of our time has reduced (and confused) the influence of economic conditions on US elections.

In September of 2024, in the waning weeks of the Joe Biden presidency, 65% of Republicans believed the US economy was getting worse. About six months later, as Donald Trump launched a trade war on the rest of the world with his “liberation day” tariffs, the share of Republican pessimists had dropped to 33%.

Continue reading...
title: Bad news for Trump ahead of the midterms: it’s still the economy, stupid

author: Heather Stewart in Bangkok
description:
Speaking at IMF meeting, chancellor says he will stick to fiscal rules while recognising business and living costs

  • UK politics live – latest updates

  • Business live – latest updates

John Healey has promised to use his first budget in a fortnight’s time to offer consumers and businesses a “breathing space” while sticking to Labour’s fiscal rules.

Speaking to journalists in Bangkok, where he has been attending the International Monetary Fund annual meetings, the chancellor said he was conscious of rising costs.

Continu
title: John Healey vows to give ‘breathing space’ to consumers and businesses in first budget

author: Martin Belam
description:
President Zelenskyy accused Donald Trump of taking Russia’s side after access to the vital system was throttled. Plus, a happy ending for a dog that was missing for a month

Good morning. Ukraine’s president has said he feels “betrayed” by Donald Trump over a throttling of Starlink access. Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused the US president of picking the other side after more than four years of war, risking a breakdown in US-Ukraine relations.

Ukraine’s military reported that the communications system, produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, was no longer working on terminals moving at speeds greater than 100mph. That effectively rendered most of the drones used by Ukraine to strike behind the frontlines inoperable and affected the country’s best air defence system to stop Russian jet-powered attack drones bombing Kyiv.
title: First Thing: US ‘betrayal’ over Starlink undermines Ukrainian defense

author: Tom Burgis in Belgrade
description:
Exclusive: Aleksandar Vučić personally intervened to push plans for controversial $500m Trump Tower in Belgrade, which sparked protests and a criminal case

Serbia’s authoritarian ruler personally intervened to advance an allegedly illegal scheme to hand over a protected site in Belgrade for a Trump tower, the Guardian can reveal.

Aleksandar Vučić summoned officials to a meeting at his presidential offices about the project, which has culminated in a landmark indictment of senior figures from his regime on charges of abuse of public office.

Continue reading...
title: Revealed: Serbian ruler’s secret role in ‘illegal’ effort to help Trump business

author: Taz Ali
description:
Donaldson has been found guilty of 18 counts of sexual abuse against two women when they were children and has been told he faces a lengthy jail term

Jeffrey Donaldson, the former leader of the Democratic Unionist party (DUP) in Northern Ireland, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for historical sexual offences against two women when they were children.

Donaldon, who led the DUP from 2021 until 2024, was convicted in June of one count of rape, 13 counts of indecent assault and four counts of gross indecency for crimes committed between 1985 and 2008.

Continue reading...
title: Former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson to be sentenced for child sexual abuse – latest updates

author: Siraj Datoo
description:
The US president said that the war will end ‘as soon as I want it to end’ as the midterms take place under a cloud of economic uncertainty

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email to get newsletter alerts in your inbox

US president Donald Trump claimed the Iran war ‘will end very soon,’ as voters consider their options ahead of midterm elections that are taking place amid economic uncertainty and ongoing global conflict.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday evening,
title: Donald Trump claims ‘Iran war will end very soon’ as midterm rallies heat up – US politics live

author: Andrew Roth in Kyiv
description:
Moscow sends swarms of drones to attack infrastructure in central Ukraine as Zelenskyy says Kyiv will restart strikes on Russian oil refineries

  • Europe live – latest updates

The White House’s unilateral effort to negotiate an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine has collapsed as Moscow sent a record swarm of drones overnight to attack infrastructure in central Ukraine and Kyiv appeared to resume strikes on Russian oil refineries – despite warnings from Donald Trump.

Moscow accused Ukraine of launching its first strike against a Russian oil refinery in the Ryazan region since Trump abruptly declared an “energy ceasefire” that neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to. Trump has demande
title: Russia and Ukraine resume energy strikes despite Trump warnings

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Exclusive: Trump has falsely claimed Afrikaners are facing ‘white genocide’, but very few have applied to live in US

The US government could spend hundreds of thousands of dollars on a media campaign in South Africa to figure out why more white Afrikaners are not applying to become refugees to the US, as Donald Trump had hoped.

State department officials, according to an August proposal seen by the Guardian, outlined a roughly $335,000 research and advertising effort after applications to the refugee program “trended lower than expected” since Afrikaners were allowed to apply directly online in November 2025. The document, written by the US mission in South Africa with a department research unit for the embassy in Pretoria, admits officials know little about why.

Continue reading...
title: US officials considering ad campaign to urge South African Afrikaners to emigrate

author: Lauren Aratani in New York
description:
Nearly 61% believe country is in recession and 65% of independents say economy is worse, according to new Harris poll

  • Send us your questions on how the US economy is shaping the midterm elections

With the midterm elections less than three weeks away, key voting groups including independents, rural voters and even some Republicans are increasingly disenchanted with Donald Trump’s economy, according to an exclusive Harris poll for the Guardian.

The majority of those surveyed were pessimistic about the economy, with three quarters of Americans saying they are concerned about a recession while 61% wrongly believe that the US is already experiencing one. By its typical definition, the US is not currently experiencing a recession.

Continue reading...
title: Key US voters say economy is getting worse ahead of midterms, exclusive poll finds

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Move comes after east African country abruptly withdrew returns cooperation earlier this year

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Eritreans could be stopped from coming to the UK unless the country agrees to accept more rejected asylum seekers and criminals, Shabana Mahmood has warned.

VIPs and officials from the east African country have already been stripped of fast-track access to UK visas after their government refused to cooperate with the return of its nationals, the home secretary said.

Continue reading...
title: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over returns policy

author: Frances Mao
description:
Charity commissioner to use speech to say there is a difference between ‘heated discussion’ and harassment or abuse

Reform leader Nigel Farage has postponed a major announcement that was due to take place in Essex this morning after an ITV investigation aired last night showing party councillors and election candidates making graphic threats of extreme violence and expressing racist and misogynistic views.

Three councillors have already stood down from the party, which said it was conducting an investigation over the first revelations from the ITV undercover investigation.

More are expected from the undercover filming of senior Reform politicians and officials working at its UK headquarters.

Continue reading...
title: Charity watchdog to criticise ‘intimidation’ after Farage calls for prosecution of groups helping asylum seekers – UK politics live

author: Kalyeena Makortoff
description:
Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as global investors fret over potential interest rate hikes

  • Business news – live updates

  • Larry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through. But a storm is coming

An accelerating sell-off of AI-linked shares has hit global markets, as fears over rising inflation and future interest rate hikes spooked traders already wary of the heavily indebted sector.

South Korea’s benchmark Kospi 200 index, which is heavily skewed towards the companies that make memory chips, fell more than 8% overnight to a six-mon
title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt

author: Josh Butler
description:
Vice Adm Buckley calls incident an ‘act of sexual violence’ and a ‘despicable betrayal of trust’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The defence department says a member of the Australian Defence Force is a “person of interest” in investigations after a video recording device was found in a bathroom on HMAS Leeuwin, in what the chief of navy called a “despicable betrayal of trust”.

A day after senator Jacqui Lambie told the Senate that a hidden camera had been found in a female shower facility onboard the naval ship, docked in Cairns, navy chief Matt Buckley confirmed a “video re
title: ADF member ‘person of interest’ after video recorder found in HMAS Leeuwin women’s showers

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Animation studio narrows annual loss to £1.1m amid ‘challenging market’ in children’s content

Don’t break out the celebratory Wensleydale just yet. Aardman, the British animation studio behind the cheese-loving inventor Wallace and his beloved dog Gromit, has fallen short of a target to get back in the black, its accounts show.

The employee-owned business was aiming to record a small profit in 2025 after two years of consecutive losses but was hit by production delays and a “challenging market” in children’s content.

Continue reading...
title: Wallace & Gromit maker Aardman falls short of return to profit

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Inquest into death of Queensland girl denied insulin by her religious parents is told Kerrie Struhs believed God would heal her daughter

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Doctors were so concerned about the religious beliefs of Elizabeth Struhs’ mother they recommended she be subjected to an involuntary mental health assessment because she delusionally believed her daughter would be healed from type 1 diabetes, a coroner has heard.

Child safety officers, nonetheless, decided to return the eight-year-old home to live with her mother, Kerrie Struhs, over the objections of Brisbane-
title: Doctors treating Elizabeth Struhs recommended involuntary mental health assessment of her mother, coroner hears

author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
description:
Latest data comes just two weeks before chancellor’s budget looks to help consumers traverse the cost of living crisis

The UK economy unexpectedly continued to grow in August despite a fall in consumer spending before chancellor John Healey’s budget.

Figures from the Office for National Statistics showed gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 0.1% last month, compared with 0.4% growth in July. City economists had forecast the economy would shrink by 0.1%.

Continue reading...
title: UK economy unexpectedly grows 0.1% in August despite fall in consumer spending

author: Fiona Harvey, Carmen Aguilar García and Michael Goodier
description:
Defra promised in March to work towards free access to data on large plots in England and Wales

The government has refused to say when the public will be able to freely access information about who owns large plots of land across England and Wales.

Emma Reynolds, the previous secretary of state for the environment, announced in March that the paywall protecting large amounts of the Land Registry would be partly lifted.

Continue reading...
title: No timeline for lifting Land Registry paywall as ownership remains opaque

author: Patrick Greenfield and Eve Livingston
description:
Prime minister presents new kind of challenge for SNP, and his Scottish visit will loom large over its big event

This year, even Andy Burnham is invited to the Scottish National party conference. But by the time John Swinney stands up to address members on Saturday afternoon in Aberdeen to reinvigorate the case for a second independence referendum, his party may regret giving the UK prime minister so much prominence in the conference buildup.

Burnham is expected to visit Scotland on Friday – the middle of the event – in a thinly veiled attempt to overshadow the SNP gathering. While he will be in a different venue, the former Manchester mayor’s presence in Scotland will loom large over the event. Since taking over at No 10 in July, Burnham has largely avoided direct confrontations with his political rivals, rarely attacking Nigel Farage or Kemi Badenoch. But he has taken a different approach with the Scottish first minister.
title: Burnham v Swinney: will the UK PM overshadow the SNP’s conference?

author: Michael Segalov
description:
In today’s newsletter: As Russia resists a ceasefire and Trump’s shifting priorities unsettle allies, an end to the conflict isn’t getting any closer

Good morning. In his usual asinine unconventional approach to international relations, Donald Trump announced on Sunday (via Truth Social, how else) an “ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine”, apparently without checking with either side. Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said any such deal was “news to me,” nonetheless declared he was “ready and we will accept it”. Vladimir Putin responded by blowing up some Ukrainian power plants.

This has been the tenor of much diplomacy during Trump’s tenure: false starts, U-turns, incoherent positions (and some
title: Thursday briefing: Thanks to an erratic Trump, peace in Ukraine is still far away

author: Kat Wong
description:
Stacey Parker was contacted following alleged murders, years after meeting Lamarre-Condon in Sydney and bonding over scepticism of Covid vaccines

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon asked a friend in Western Australia if he could post her a phone to be thrown into a body of water, and told her he’d been “set up” over the disappearance of two men, a court has heard.

Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird and Luke Dav
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly asked celebrity chaser friend if he could post phone to her in WA to throw in water, court told

author: Josh Butler
description:
Communications minister rebuts claims that Labor’s digital duty of care laws would lead to government control of speech

  • Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australians could still “listen to manosphere podcasts” or “say the moon landing was fake” under proposed new online safety laws, Anika Wells has stressed as she rubbished claims they would lead to government censorship

The communications minister also said she was considering updates to the digital duty of care laws to allo
title: ‘Manosphere’ podcasts and moon-landing conspiracy theories to remain online under new laws, Wells says

author: Kate Lamb and agencies
description:
Having tried cloud seeding and water bombing, one pilot project will see dry ice dispersed by plane across the province of South Sumatra

As fires ravage Indonesia, emitting a toxic smoke that has drawn the ire of regional neighbours, the government is testing an unusual new approach to tackle the haze: dry ice.

Having tried cloud seeding, water bombing and sending in army personnel to fight the fires, Indonesia’s coordinating security minister said dry ice would be dropped on the province of South Sumatra on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Out-of-pocket costs for abortion care to be covered regardless of who wins November election as Jess Wilson says Liberals and Nationals ‘will not allow Labor to play politics on this issue’

  • Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victoria will become the first state in Australia to make access to abortion care free, no matter who wins the November election, with the Coalition matching
title: Victoria to become first state to make abortions free as Coalition matches Labor election promise

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
Steele-John said he rejected the claims and had referred them to the Western Australian Greens for a ‘fair, independent process’

Greens senator Jordon Steele-John has taken leave from the party room after complaints were made, triggering an independent review.

The Nine newspapers reported on Thursday afternoon that seven party members demanded an investigation into allegations he made inappropriate comments to a number of women.

Continue reading...
title: Greens senator Jordon Steele-John takes leave amid investigation into complaints

author: Ariana Baio and Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Talarico casts himself as a moderate who would put Texans’ needs over party allegiances amid close contest against Republican Ken Paxton

James Talarico, the Texas Democratic nominee for Senate, sat face to face with several undecided voters who grilled him on a slew of contentious issues including Israel’s military campaign in Gaza, abortion and foreign aid, during a CNN town hall on Wednesday evening.

One voter, a devout small business owner, questioned the authenticity of Talarico’s faith, referencing a past remark where he described God as nonbinary.

title: Texas Democrat James Talarico faces grilling from voters at town hall in tight Senate race

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Whistleblowers applauded as Ibac finds ‘decisions were made to withhold information about the magnitude of the loss’

Senior public servants in one state covered up losses suspected to be worth hundreds of millions of dollars arising from flawed Covid-19 business support payments, an investigation has found.

During the pandemic, the Victorian government spent an estimated $257m on support grants to 9,000 ineligible businesses.

title: Senior Victorian public servants hid loss of up to $285m from Covid grants given to ineligible businesses

author: Krishani Dhanji and Tory Shepherd
description:
Liberal Paul Scarr breaks ranks to condemn major parties, saying he will write to Queensland attorney general

Labor and the Coalition have blocked a vote on a bill that would have banned the shackling of incarcerated women during childbirth, with the government saying it was the responsibility of the states and territories.

Independent senator Lidia Thorpe introduced the bills into the Senate, which would prevent shackling and stop children being strip-searched.

Continue reading...
title: Labor and Coalition block bill that would ban incarcerated women being shackled in childbirth
